# Learner help, grammar, kanji and hanzi

## Architecture rules

- **Learner data** ([details](../../docs/project/tech-stack.md#learner-languages)): bundled data files only, no library code and no download. Regenerate generated files with their `tools/` script, never hand-edit them; keep credits in `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` and the licence screen; memory stories are the project's own, never copied. Every grammar point needs its example test and its text in all 9 interface languages.

## Full text: docs/project/tech-stack.md, section 'Learner languages'

### Learner languages

- Chinese learner help (owner decision 2026-10-18, [spec](../../docs/specs/2026-10-18-chinese-learner-help.md)) bundles data files only: jieba's word list and HanLP's pinyin and traditional-to-simplified tables, extracted at build time into `assets/learner-data/` (`LearnerLanguageData` in `app/build.gradle.kts`). No jieba or HanLP code and no download. Words are spoken with Google Translate's online voice (`translation/GoogleWebSpeech.kt`) while Google translates subtitles, in every language (owner decision, [spec](../../docs/specs/2026-10-19-google-voice-every-language.md)): three Google addresses, then the phone's voices; after no address answers, the phone speaks at once for 2 minutes. Chinese grammar points (`data/ChineseGrammarCatalogue.kt` plus rules in `ChineseGrammar.kt`) share `data/GrammarMatcher.kt` with Japanese and carry HSK 3.0 levels (1–6 and 7–9) from the GF0025-2021 grammar syllabus, or the HSK 3.0 word list for points it does not list; every point needs its own example sentence in `ChineseGrammarCatalogueTest` and its text in all 9 interface languages.
- English learner help (owner request 2026-10-18, [spec](../../docs/specs/2026-10-18-english-learner-help.md)) also bundles data files only: OpenNLP's English part-of-speech model and WordNet 3.1's word and irregular-form lists, extracted at build time into `assets/learner-data/`, plus the CEFR-J word levels committed in `app/src/main/learner-data/` (free for commercial use with citation; keep the citation in `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` and the licence screen). No OpenNLP or WordNet code. English grammar points carry CEFR levels from the CEFR-J Grammar Profile (the rule is in the spec); every point needs its own example sentence in `EnglishGrammarCatalogueTest` and its text in all 9 interface languages.
- English IPA (25kiuo, #81, owner pick 2026-11-16, [spec](../../docs/specs/2026-11-16-instant-word-card-read-aloud-ipa-sleep-timer.md)): `en-ipa.txt` in `app/src/main/learner-data/`, made by `tools/english/build_english_ipa.py` from ipa-dict's American English (MIT, from cmudict-ipa and the CMU Pronouncing Dictionary) for the words of FrequencyWords' English top 50,000 (CC BY-SA 4.0: keep the credits in `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` and the licence screen; regenerate, never hand-edit). `wordReading()` in `data/EnglishIpa.kt` gives the word card and the card's Reading field the analyzer's own reading (kana, pinyin) first, else an English single word's IPA; other languages get none.
- Spanish learner help (owner request 2026-11-13, [spec](../../docs/specs/2026-11-13-spanish-learner-help.md)) bundles data files only: OpenNLP's Spanish part-of-speech model (extracted at build time) and `es-verbs.txt` / `es-words.txt` in `app/src/main/learner-data/`, generated from Wiktionary (Wiktextract) and FrequencyWords by `tools/spanish/build_spanish_data.py` (CC BY-SA 4.0: keep the credit in `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` and the licence screen; regenerate, never hand-edit; the plural rules in `tools/spanish/spanish_rules.py` and `SpanishLexicon.kt` must stay the same). Spanish grammar levels are placed by hand from the Instituto Cervantes PCIC and textbook order (see the spec); every point needs its own example sentence in `SpanishGrammarCatalogueTest` and its text in all 9 interface languages (`strings_grammar_es.xml`).
- German learner help (contributor request, mrAlishah, PR #233, [spec](../../docs/specs/2026-11-14-german-grammar.md)) bundles data files only: OpenNLP's German part-of-speech model (extracted at build time) and `de-verbs.txt` / `de-words.txt` in `app/src/main/learner-data/`, generated by `tools/german/build_german_data.py` from Wiktionary (Wiktextract) and FrequencyWords (CC BY-SA 4.0: keep the credit in `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` and the licence screen; regenerate, never hand-edit; the weak-verb rules in the script and `GermanConjugation.kt` must stay the same). German grammar never calls an AI; every point needs its example in `GermanGrammarTest` / `GermanRulePointsTest`, its level in `GERMAN_RULE_LEVELS` and its text in all 9 interface languages (`strings_grammar_de.xml`). Points made of words that are not next to each other use `GrammarMatch.evidence`.
- Kanji details on the word card (owner request 2026-10-24, [spec](../../docs/specs/2026-10-24-word-meaning-and-kanji-details.md)) bundle data files only in `app/src/main/learner-data/`: `ja-kanji.txt` and `ja-kanji-strokes.txt` are made by `tools/kanji/build_kanji_data.py` from KANJIDIC2 and KanjiVG and stay CC BY-SA (keep the credits in `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` and the licence screen; Hán Việt corrections go in the script's `HAN_VIET_FIXES`). `ja-radicals.txt` and the memory stories `ja-kanji-stories-en.txt` / `-vi.txt` are the project's own (MIT): never copy WaniKani, Koohii or Kanji alive mnemonics. Every jōyō kanji needs both stories (`JapaneseKanjiTest`); a Vietnamese story names a Hán Việt reading in capitals.
- Chinese character details (owner request 2026-10-24, [spec](../../docs/specs/2026-10-24-chinese-character-details.md)) share the "Character details" setting with kanji. `zh-hanzi.txt`, `zh-hanzi-strokes.txt` and `zh-hanviet.txt` are made by `tools/hanzi/build_hanzi_data.py` from Make Me a Hanzi (strokes: Arphic Public License, keep the change notice in the file; facts: LGPL-3+), HSK 3.0 (ivankra/hsk30, MIT), Unihan and KANJIDIC2; Hán Việt corrections go in the script's `HAN_VIET_FIXES`. The stories `zh-hanzi-stories-en.txt` / `-vi.txt` are the project's own (MIT): never copy Remembering the Hanzi, Mandarin Blueprint, Outlier or Skritter mnemonics. Every HSK character needs both stories, a story uses only the character and its own parts as Chinese characters, and a Vietnamese story names the Hán Việt reading in capitals when there is one (`ChineseCharactersTest`).
